subject: Information Theory
title: DNS: The Internet's Phone Book
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: DNS: The Internet's Phone Book.

hook.text: You type google.com and your browser contacts 142.250.80.46. DNS translated the name in about 20 milliseconds.

buildup.text: The Domain Name System maps human-readable names to IP addresses through a hierarchical distributed database.

discovery.text: DNS queries cascade: root servers point to TLD servers, which point to authoritative servers for each domain.

twist.text: DNS was designed in 1983 with minimal security. DNS spoofing lets attackers redirect traffic to malicious servers.

climax.text: DNSSEC adds cryptographic signatures to DNS responses—error correction for the internet's address book.

punchline.text: Names to numbers in milliseconds. DNS makes the internet usable.

quiz.question: What does DNS do?
options: Translates domain names to IP addresses
